title: The Quiet Splash

topics.value_lesson: The quiet joy of saying hello to a new friend

spine: A storyteller remembers waiting on a warm rock for the tide pool to wake up, and the small hellos that came with the light.

pool_name.role: What the child calls the tide pool

segments.text: I remember a morning, little one, when you and I sat on a big warm rock. The sun had baked it cozy, like toast. Below us lay {pool_name}, still and clear as bathwater. We wiggled our toes. We waited. The sun spilled a golden ripple across the water. Shiver-shine. Shiver-shine. "Is anyone home?" you whispered. I listened. You listened. The pool went blub. Just one little blub. Somebody was waking up down there.

Then the sand goes puff. Up rises the octopus, slow and wiggly. One arm lifts. Then another. Curl. Uncurl. Each arm waves all by itself, like eight little hellos. You wiggle your fingers back. The golden ripple grows brighter. Shiver-shine. Shiver-shine. "Hello, wiggly one," you say. The octopus waves. We wave. But where is the little fish? We listen. We wait.

Then a silver fish darts in. Quick, quick, quick. It swims in small circles, round and round. Then it stops. It opens its mouth. Blub. Blub. Tiny bubbles float up, up, up. Pop at the top. "Blub blub," you say. The fish blows more bubbles. The golden ripple grows brighter. Shiver-shine. Shiver-shine. We watch the bubbles dance. But where is the wiggly octopus? We look. We wait.

"What did you find?" I whisper. You wiggle your fingers. "Come and see!" And here they are, both friends together in {pool_name}. The octopus waves one arm, slow and sleepy. Hello. Hello. The little fish blows bubbles that float up, up, past its wiggly arms. Blub. Blub. Then, from under a pink coral branch, a tiny pink crab peeks out. It waves one little claw sideways. Hello to you too! Far away, a big whale hums a low, rumbly song. The water shivers gently. The golden ripple grows brighter on the sandy bottom. Shiver-shine. Shiver-shine. But the light is shifting now. Our quiet splash is beginning to pass.

You wiggle your fingers at the little fish. Wiggle, wiggle. It blows one last big bubble. Pop! The octopus waves one arm, slow and sleepy. Bye-bye. Bye-bye. We sit on our warm rock a little longer. The sun-baked stone feels cozy under us. The golden ripple fades, soft and low. Shiver-shine. Shiver-shine. "Do you hear it?" I whisper. Blub. Blub. The sound stays in your ears. We carry it home with us, all the way back. Eight arms waving. One little fish saying blub. You wiggle your fingers again, just to remember.

You blow a gentle kiss toward the water. Mwah. The octopus curls one arm into a soft spiral, like a hug. The little fish swims one last slow circle. Round and round. We sit on our warm rock a little longer. The sun-baked stone feels cozy under us. The golden ripple fades, soft and low. Shiver-shine. Shiver-shine. "Do you see it?" I whisper. The light shimmers on the sandy bottom. We carry the picture home with us, all the way back. One curled arm. One slow circle. You blow another kiss, just to remember.
